In [[algebra]], the '''congruence ideal''' of a [[Surjective function|surjective]] [[ring homomorphism]] ''f''&nbsp;:&nbsp;''B''&nbsp;→&nbsp;''C'' of [[commutative ring]]s is the [[Image (mathematics)|image]] under ''f'' of the [[Annihilator (ring theory)|annihilator]] of the [[Kernel (algebra)|kernel]] of&nbsp;''f''.

It is called a congruence ideal because when ''B'' is a [[Hecke algebra]] and ''f'' is a homomorphism corresponding to a [[modular form]], the congruence ideal describes congruences between the modular form of ''f'' and other modular forms.

==Example==
* Suppose ''C'' and ''D'' are rings with homomorphisms to a ring ''E'', and let ''B'' = ''C''×<sub>''E''</sub>''D'' be the pullback, given by the subring of ''C''×''D'' of pairs (''c'',''d'') where ''c'' and ''d'' have the same image in ''E''. If ''f'' is the natural projection from ''B'' to ''C'', then the kernel is the ideal ''J'' of elements (0,''d'') where ''d'' has image 0 in ''E''. If ''J'' has annihilator 0 in ''D'', then its annihilator in ''B'' is just the kernel ''I'' of the map from ''C'' to ''E''. So the congruence ideal of ''f'' is the ideal (''I'',0) of ''B''.
* Suppose that ''B'' is the [[Hecke algebra]] generated by [[Hecke operator]]s ''T''<sub>''n''</sub> acting on the 2-dimensional space of modular forms of level 1 and weight 12.This space is 2 dimensional, spanned by the Eigenforms given by the [[Eisenstein series]] ''E''<sub>12</sub> and the [[modular discriminant]] Δ. The map taking a Hecke operator ''T''<sub>''n''</sub> to its eigenvalues (σ<sub>11</sub>(''n''),τ(''n'')) gives a homomorphism from ''B'' into the ring '''Z'''×'''Z''' (where τ is the [[Ramanujan tau function]] and σ<sub>11</sub>(''n'') is the sum of the 11th powers of the divisors of ''n''). The image is the set of pairs (''c'',''d'') with ''c'' and ''d''  congruent mod 619 because of Ramanujan's congruence σ<sub>11</sub>(''n'') ≡ τ(''n'') mod 691. If ''f'' is the homomorphism taking (''c'',''d'') to ''c'' in '''Z''', then the congruence ideal is (691). So the congruence ideal describes the congruences between the forms  ''E''<sub>12</sub> and Δ.
